_README: Every actorId and every field name below is UNVERIFIED. apify.com was unreachable
from the environment this was built in, so nothing here was checked against a live
actor. Run `npm run probe-actor -- <source>` with APIFY_TOKEN set: it runs the actor
once, saves the raw dataset to .probe/, and prints the real field inventory.
Then correct `input.fields` and `map` here. No code change is needed for a remap.
input.fields maps our canonical knob -> the actor's own input key. null means the
actor does not support that knob; the pipeline filters client-side where it can.
map values are ordered candidate paths (dot notation, [n] for array index). The first
path that yields a non-empty value wins, so listing several variants keeps a run alive
through minor actor changes. A miss on a `required` field aborts that source loudly.

upwork.verified_at: 2026-09-07, ran but returned unrelated results; query field corrected from searchQuery to queries

unmapped_knobs.note: Documented on the actor but not wired up. Budget Range is the interesting one: filtering low budgets at the source would stop us paying for $5 postings at all.

upwork.blocked: Input field names unknown. searchQuery and queries were both accepted and silently ignored ("No queries provided, fetching all jobs"), so every run returns arbitrary listings. Waiting on the schema dump from the next probe.

linkedin.pricing_note: Pay per result, and dedupes server-side. Third LinkedIn actor tried: the first was a rental, the second is retired.

rejected.bebity/linkedin-jobs-scraper: $29.99/month rental, fixed fee outside the budget cap
rejected.smorgi_apps/linkedin-jobs-scraper: Permanently offline. Actor throws on start: "residential + Playwright unit economics; historical success below the keep gate. Not scheduled to return."

linkedin.blocked: Enforces maxItems >= 150 per query. At roughly $6/1k that is about $0.90 a query against a $0.60 cap for the whole run, so the budget guard would refuse every query and the source would silently never run. Needs a cost decision.
linkedin.schema_notes: Rich schema. Useful and safe: publishedAt (r86400/r604800/r2592000), jobTitleExclude, excludeRecruitingAgencies, companySizeMin/Max, workType. salaryBase (enum up to 120000) matches the salary floor exactly but is NOT wired on purpose: LinkedIn salary filters act on stated salary, so it would drop every posting that omits pay, which is most of the good ones, and that contradicts the rule that missing compensation never rejects.

indeed.schema_notes: Declared inputs: position, maxItemsPerSearch, country, location, parseCompanyDetails, saveOnlyUniqueItems, followApplyRedirects, startUrls. We had been sending maxItems and maxDaysOld, neither of which is declared. There is no recency input at all, so freshness is client-side only and daily runs will re-fetch the same top results. That is the duplicate billing the spend report tracks.
